title: WISE 0855
blurb: The coldest brown dwarf known. Too faint for one exposure — until they are added up.
story: WISE 0855 is the coldest brown dwarf known: colder than ice, and only about 7 light-years away. In a single two-minute SPHEREx exposure it barely rises out of the noise. Here every visit's exposures are added together, and a faint dot appears in the cross-hair. Blink the visits: it steps toward the west, about 8 arcseconds a year. Blink X found it by itself this way.

spectrum.hint: It is faint: every dot is one noisy exposure, so the line joins the middle value of each 9 neighbouring measurements. From 4.42 to 5.00 µm no clear change of brightness stands out of the noise.

doodles.explain: Too faint to stand out in a single exposure, this one appears when each visit's exposures are added together. It slides steadily toward the west: 9.2 arcseconds (1.5 SPHEREx pixels) in 12 months, about 9.4 arcseconds a year. Steady drift like this is how a nearby star or brown dwarf looks from Earth. (Something this close also wobbles with the seasons, by up to an arcsecond: over a year or so that wobble is part of the number.) This is WISEA J085510.74-071442.5, a known brown dwarf (SIMBAD). The catalogue lists 8.15 arcseconds a year; these images give 9.4 ± 0.9.

source: NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx Level-2 spectral images (collections spherex_dr1, spherex_qr3)
